extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys/agents, and students learning patent drafting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing a patent application that complies with patent law and is well suited to obtain protection for an invention; covers drafting goals, process steps, conventions, term-meanings, and prosecution planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement (sufficient disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discloses the invention sufficiently that a person of ordinary skill in the art can make and use it (enablement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail, examples, working parameters, and embodiments so a skilled practitioner can reproduce and use the invention without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written description (possession of the invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrates the inventor was in possession of the invention as claimed (written description).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the invention and its aspects clearly and specifically so the disclosure supports the full scope of the claimed subject matter; include support for claim limitations and variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the invention in claims of appropriate scope, neither too broad (invalid over prior art) nor too narrow (easily designed around).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance breadth and patentability: draft claims wide enough to be meaningful but with support and distinctions over prior art; include fallback narrower claim sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid estoppels
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoids estoppels that would limit later claim construction or assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious in specification and prosecution statements that could later be used to narrow claim interpretation; avoid admissions of intent or limitation unless necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention disclosure interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventor meets with attorney to explain the invention (invention disclosure interview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a thorough interview to capture inventive concepts, alternatives, problems solved, implementation details, and possible variants — this forms the basis of the disclosure and claim strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art search
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the closest known references (prior art search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search relevant literature and patents to locate closest references, inform claim scope, and guide distinguishing language and fallback positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Draft independent and dependent claims of varying scope (claim drafting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include multiple independent claims (different statutory categories where appropriate) and dependent claims that narrow on legally meaningful dimensions to provide layered protection and prosecution flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification drafting (support claim terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write specification supporting all claim terms (specification drafting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every claim term has support in the specification (definitions, embodiments, examples) and that the spec provides enablement and written description for claimed ranges and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare formal patent drawings (drawings preparation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, labeled figures with reference numbers matching the specification; drawings should illustrate embodiments and elements referred to in claims and description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple drafts; cross-check claims against spec for support (review and revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iteratively revise claims and specification, checking antecedent basis, terminology consistency, and that claim scope is supported; use internal reviews to catch gaps or limiting language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single sentence claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim is a single sentence, however long (single sentence claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose claims as one sentence with correct punctuation and structure; avoid splitting claim elements into multiple sentences which may cause drafting or interpretation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: First mention of an element uses 'a' or 'an'; subsequent mentions use 'the' or 'said' (antecedent basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear antecedent basis to avoid ambiguity in claim elements; ensure each term is introduced before being referred to with definite articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: One term per concept throughout the application (consistent terminology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same term to refer to the same concept across claims and specification to avoid confusion or unintended narrowing; avoid introducing multiple synonyms for the same element unless defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice for method steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Method steps use active verbs (active voice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft method claims and descriptions in active voice where appropriate to clearly attribute actions to the actor or apparatus and to improve clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference numbers tied to figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each element in the spec is given a number that ties to the figures (reference numbers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign consistent reference numerals in the specification and drawings to make element references unambiguous and to support claim interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No marketing language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid superlatives and promotional terms (no marketing language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude marketing phrases or unsupported claims of superiority (e.g., 'best', 'superior') since they may introduce unintended limitations or provide no technical disclosure value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Words to avoid ('Patent Profanity')
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid words that create inferred limitations or unwanted legal effects, such as 'essential', 'critical', 'necessary', 'must', 'always', 'never', 'the invention is', 'the present invention requires', 'object of the invention', 'preferred', and 'only'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These terms can suggest limitation, exclusion, or required features; prefer neutral descriptive language and explicitly describe alternatives rather than using absolute qualifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprising (open transitional phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Comprising': Open transitional phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'comprising' to indicate the claimed device/process includes the recited elements but may include additional elements; choose transitions deliberately to control claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting of (closed transitional phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Consisting of': Closed transitional phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'consisting of' to limit the claim to the listed elements only; recognize it excludes unrecited elements and therefore narrows scope sharply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consisting essentially of (semi-closed transitional phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Consisting essentially of': Semi-closed transitional phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'consisting essentially of' to allow only unrecited elements that do not materially affect the basic and novel properties of the invention; it's intermediate between 'comprising' and 'consisting of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means for (invoke 35 U.S.C. §112(f) in US)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Means for': Invokes 35 USC 112(f) in US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid or use 'means for' clauses with care: they can trigger means-plus-function claim treatment, which constrains the claim to the structures disclosed in the specification that perform the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: About/approximately/substantially (require spec support)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'About,' 'approximately,' 'substantially': Allowed but require spec support to avoid indefiniteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using imprecise qualifiers, provide examples, ranges, or tolerances in the specification to give objective boundaries and avoid indefiniteness challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality defined
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Plurality' means 'two or more' (plurality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using terms like 'plurality', ensure the specification and claims make clear what numerical range is intended (e.g., two or more) to prevent ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiment disclosure (multiple embodiments and alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose multiple embodiments of the invention, including alternative materials, geometries, processes, and ranges (embodiment disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide alternative implementations, materials, parameter ranges, and fallback features to support broader claim construction and to provide prosecution fallback positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim hierarchy (independent and dependent claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical strong patent has several independent claims (covering method, system, apparatus, etc.) with dependent claims that narrow on legally meaningful dimensions (claim hierarchy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft independent claims to cover different statutory categories and include dependent claims that add specific limitations, preferred ranges, or optional features to preserve enforceable fallbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation practice (planning for continuations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for continuation applications, which allow the applicant to pursue different claim scopes in subsequent applications based on the same disclosure (continuation practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the disclosure and claim sets to enable future continuations: disclose alternatives and claim-supporting details now so later filings can pursue broader or different scopes without new matter issues.
